title: Two vendor names look identical but Excel won't match them

payoff.headline:
One space
you can't see
kills the match
payoff.sub: Wrap the exported value in TRIM before you compare it or look it up.

script.vo: Two vendor names read exactly the same, and Excel tells you they're different.
Vendor names off the AP aging export.
script.caption:
Vendor names off the
AP aging export.

script.vo: The vendor master sits right underneath, with terms on it.
script.caption:
The master list is
right underneath.

script.vo: Simplest test there is. Top name against the master name.
script.caption:
Straight comparison.
Top name against master.

script.vo: Both cells read Northwind Logistics. Nothing is misspelled. The export just left a space hanging off the end of the first one, and that space counts as a character.
script.caption:
There's a space
hanging off the end.

script.vo: So wrap the exported value in TRIM. It clears spaces off both ends and collapses any doubles in the middle.
script.caption: Wrap it in *TRIM*.

script.vo: One caveat. TRIM only handles the regular space. Data pasted out of a browser or a PDF often carries a non breaking space, and TRIM leaves that one sitting there.
script.caption:
TRIM misses non breaking
spaces from web pastes.

script.vo: Fill it down and the rest of the vendors tie out.
script.caption: Fill down. All match.

script.vo: A space you can't see still counts. Trim it before you compare anything.

post.title: Two vendor names look identical but Excel says they don't match
post.description:
excel says two identical text values don't match
AP exports often carry a trailing space on the vendor name, so the comparison comes back FALSE. Wrap the exported value in TRIM and it matches. Save this for close.
